about: A dark fantasy, desktop-companion incremental idle game about a Knight cursed with immortality.  The Knight clashes against endless waves of undead, but for what? The memories, the reasons, The Order they swore themselves to, all faded to dust long ago. Now they simply fight, die, and rise. Again, and again, and again.  Yet, the fleeting flames of Remembrance have begun to spark. Unravel the mystery of the Knight's immortality curse, piece together a tattered past, and perhaps grant them the chance to break the Cycle of Undeath once and for all.   A endless battle against the undead in the corner of your screen   Infi-Knight lives in a resizable, movable window beside your other tasks. Look over to tithe your Gold, swap a Weapon, ignite a surge of  Zeal , or unlock what the Knight has remembered in the  Memory  codex.           Death rejects you   The Knight has one hit point and has been curse-bound to never truly die. Sooner or later, the horde   will   reach them. The Knight will fall, and rise, and fight again.  However ,   nothing is lost   when the Knight dies: every coin and every XP orb gained from the undead contributes to the Knight's growing power.  Immortality  is your punishment and  penance .            A worthy arsenal    Ten Weapons , each with their own way of unmaking the undead. A lane-clearing Halberd, a Holy Mace blessed by God, a full-field Arbalest, a burning Lance that sweeps across the horde, a massive Greatsword to cleave the graves, and more. Every kill contributes to that weapon's   Mastery  , a system that rewards sticking with a specific weapon to unlock passive upgrades with powerful  Tier 5  and  10    Capstone Perks   that  change the way each weapon plays .            Steadily grow your power   As The Knight stands against the undead, they collect  XP orbs  and gain up to  99   Levels    to fuel their baseline power and unlock  new gameplay  features.            Swear your Oath and gather lost Relics   Swear one of six   Oaths  , each a bargain to be weighed. Equip   Relics   that pair with your Weapon and Oath to create your very own build with which to stand against the endless undead.           Rekindle Memories to uncover your past   Reach milestones to reawaken your history as a Knight of  The Order.  With rekindled memories come new  Weapons ,  Relics ,  Lore  and more.             Gather Embers from Bosses   Pry valuable  Embers  from the bones of  Bosses . Then, spend them by performing   Last Rites   to gain permanent upgrades back at your  Camp .           Restore your Camp   Your hard-won  Embers  are consumed at  Camp,  which   provides you with   permanent meta-progression   that unlocks   new gameplay   elements and steadily improves your power.                A long incremental game with a Story Mode ending, and an unlockable Endless Mode.   Dozens of  Memories  across four acts, rekindled by your milestones and accomplishments. Piece together who the Knight was, the nature of their Immortality Curse, what their Order did, and why the dead will not remain buried.       A true desktop companion incremental idler. Resizable, borderless, option for always-on-top. Built to live beside your other tasks.     10 Weapons  with per-weapon  Mastery  ranks and  transformative   Capstone perks      14 Relics  to collect with build-changing passives     6   Oaths  to swear, each with an upside and downside to weigh    A  Camp  permanent meta-progression upgrade system     250 Levels  to attain     Dozens of   Memories  telling a four-act dark fantasy story in fragments     Dozens of hours  of gameplay    Unlockable  Infinite Mode      A global  Leaderboard  to rank each faithful Knight     An ending that may just solve the Immortality Curse       Capsule illustration credit -  Rodrigo Balmaceda

short: Dogs walk around on your desktop. A dog is loyal to its owner — unlike a cat, it actually does as it's told. Put two out and they'll greet each other and play chase. A resident pet app with a free base version. Please take good care of them.
about: Sill Dogs is a resident desktop pet app where dogs live on your screen. Not inside a window — they walk directly across whatever you have open right now. The base app is free.     You can have up to two dogs on screen. With two of them out, they notice each other, come over, say hello, and start a game of chase. Enjoy watching them behave like real dogs.  Two dogs you get for free  The small, adorable Beagle (tricolor)  The big, dependable German Shepherd (black)     Paid DLC adds more breeds.    How they spend the day changes with the hour  Dogs are animals that fall in step with their owner's life. Their activity peaks in the morning and the evening, the daytime passes with short rests in between, and late at night they sleep soundly. They won't tear around at midnight the way a cat does. Now and then, though, a dog will break into a run at dawn or dusk for no reason at all.    They talk with their tails  A dog's feelings show in its tail. Wagging while sitting, wagging while lying down, wagging faster when excited, wagging hardest of all at a reunion. Even the same "tail wag" looks different depending on the moment.     Walking on your windows  Dogs use your open windows as footholds — walking along them, jumping down, climbing back up. Whatever state your desktop is in becomes their playground.     Staying out of your way  A desktop pet, however cute, gets removed the moment it gets in the way of your work. Sill Dogs lets you adjust the following in the settings.       Reaction to the cursor  /  Reaction to clicks  — each can be set to "Off / Weak / Normal / Strong".  The default is "Weak" .    Set it to "Off" and the dogs won't come over to your cursor while you're working    An option to keep the dogs off the front of a display while you're playing a full-screen game or watching a full-screen video    Dog size, which screen they appear on, and how many dogs (one or two)    You can move the dogs by dragging them      How to change the settings  Changing the breed, choosing which screen they appear on, quitting the app — all of it is done from the icon in the notification area (system tray), or from the bone sign.       Find the Sill Dogs icon in the Windows notification area and  right-click  it to open the menu    If you can't find the icon, click the "^" button at the bottom right of the screen to see the hidden icons    You can also open the settings screen from the "bone sign" on your screen.    From the menu you can choose "Breed selection", "Number of dogs", "Screen settings", "Auto-start settings", "Setting" and "Quit Sill Dogs"       About the DLC  Adding more breeds requires paid DLC.  There is a free toy DLC as well.  There is currently no feature for showing three or more dogs at once.  About the pixel art  The dogs' pixel art uses assets drawn by the pixel artist girlypixels.       Other  If you find a bug, reporting it on the Community Hub discussion board would be a great help.     Even if you live somewhere you can't keep a dog, even while you're working. Over in the corner of your screen, a dog is going about its usual day.  A link-up with our sister apps Sill Cats and Sill Sticks is in the works. It may take a little while. lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Simplified Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Finnish, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese - Portugal, Russian, Turkish
short: A tiny medieval village lives on top of your taskbar. Every file you delete falls from the sky, and its little villagers turn your digital trash into new ideas, buildings and festivals. Watch a lone campfire grow into a walled town while you work.
about: A village that lives on your desktop     Townlet is a tiny pixel-art village that lives in a thin strip just above your Windows taskbar. It only shows when your desktop does, never steals focus and never pops up notifications. Seven-pixel villagers chop wood, hammer at the forge, gossip in the square and head home when night falls, while you get on with your day.            Your trash is their treasure     Every time you delete a file, it drops into the village from the sky. The villagers carry it to the square, study it and turn it into knowledge. Pictures inspire artists, documents fill the scribe's shelves, music brings minstrels to town. Discoveries unlock new buildings, decorations and events, so no two villages grow the same way. Townlet never opens, moves or deletes your files. It only notices what kind of file landed in the Recycle Bin and how big it was. Nothing ever leaves your computer.                From campfire to walled town     Start with a single campfire and grow through village, town and city into a walled town with its own castle               Real seasons and a real day-night cycle: blossoms in spring, snow in winter, lantern light at night  Rain, storms, fog and starry skies                Markets, fairs, a town crier with the news, travelling minstrels and many small surprises             Pick up a villager and drop them somewhere else, just to see what they say              Decorate the village your way and design its banner              Keep a village ledger of your discoveries, history and the events you've seen  Take a picture of your village and share it     Calm by design     Nothing ever goes wrong in Townlet. No deaths, no famine, no fires, no lost progress. The village only ever grows. A soft seasonal soundtrack plays while your desktop is in view, and the village quietly fades out the moment you open a full-screen window.

Royalty-free tracks  (260 TRACKS!)  by talented independent artists.     Ambience mixer  — rain, forest, ocean, fireplace, wind, whatever puts you in the zone. Quick tools  — sticky notes, a to-do list with  daily streaks , clipboard history, whiteboard scratchpad — all one click away. Or attach the full window to the left or right edge of your monitor as a permanent productivity sidebar — your office, your timer, your stats, always glanceable. Optional purchases are not required and can further increase the Auto Repeat limit or improve expedition efficiency.  No ads are displayed in the Steam version.  Text size can be adjusted from 0.8x to 2.0x, and the window can be freely resized.   ◆ Artesnaut: Hardcore Idle Fantasy RPG   Experience a deep story of adventure with characters YOU create! Select from myriad jobs, races, and skills to build your perfect party!  A hack & slash idle RPG in a captivating fantasy world! Build a party of unique characters and conquer dungeons! Ask for an internet search, set a timer, or start a Pomodoro session in natural language. Optional desktop tools and integrations are used only when you enable them. Vision Capabilities:  Aifu can analyze what you see. Provide screenshots or paste images directly into the chat for your companion to process, analyze, and comment on. short: A hero who lives above your taskbar. Keepwatch is an idle auto-battler RPG that quietly runs on your desktop — build your camp, gear up your one and only hero, and let them fight while you get back to work.
about: A world that lives on your desktop     Keepwatch: Idle Kingdom RPG is a medieval auto-battler that lives right above your Windows taskbar. You command a single hero — but not directly. They wander, work, grow, and fight incoming enemies on their own. Your role is to grow your camp, make gear and skill decisions, and step in at critical moments.    The game stays open on your desktop until you close it. It runs quietly in the background at its own pace, never interrupting your real work — but there's always something happening if you glance over.                 One hero, one path!            There's no class selection — a single archetype. What makes your build interesting doesn't come from a character creation screen, it comes from  your skill tree and the gear you find . Your hero grows stronger by leveling up, but the real difference comes from your armor, your weapon, and the skill choices you make. By day, your hero works around camp, gathers resources, and builds. When night falls, the real threat begins: waves of enemies march on your camp, and your hero fights them automatically.                   Build your camp, grow your kingdom!      Five different buildings, each upgradeable up to ten tiers:  Home, Blacksmith, Kitchen, Workshop, Vault.  Each gives your hero a different edge — passive experience, crafting recipes, storage capacity, or gear upgrades. The more you develop your buildings, the stronger the gear your hero can access.       Home    Blacksmith    Kitchen              Your hero passively earns experience here while idle around camp.            The heart of weapon and armor upgrades — higher tiers raise your success chance.            Recipes crafted here feed your hero's endurance and recovery.      Workshop    Vault                  The crafting hub for clothing, bags, and potions.            Keep your inventory and gold safely stored.             Automatic combat, real tension!      The moment your hero spots an enemy, they fight — closing the distance, attacking, and using skills automatically. Your job is preparing the right gear and skill tree; your hero handles the rest.            Three tiers, one glance to read  Every enemy silhouette tells you everything you need to know before the fight starts:     Raider  — light, narrow, unarmored. Fast and weak on their own, dangerous in a crowd.     Soldier  — mid-sized, partial armor, often carries a shield. The baseline threat once your camp is established.     Champion  — broad-shouldered, fully armored, slow but hits hard and soaks up damage.    No health bars to squint at — silhouette alone tells you what you're facing at a glance.  Ten cultures, one battlefield    Every enemy tier comes reskinned across ten distinct cultures — Arabian, British, Chinese, Frank, Holy Roman, Iberian, Japanese, Roman, Turkish, and Viking — drawn at random per spawn. A night wave can throw a Viking raider and a Japanese raider at you side by side. Culture is purely cosmetic: it never changes stats, weapons, or behavior, so the only thing you ever need to read off an enemy is its silhouette.       Arabian    British    Chinese    Frank    Holy Roman                                                          Iberian    Japanese    Roman    Turkish    Viking                                                           Weapons and range are never fixed    Enemies don't carry a hardcoded loadout. On spawn, each one draws from its tier's weapon pool — the same weapon catalog your hero uses — which also decides whether it's carrying a shield and what level its weapon sits at. Anyone wielding a bow or crossbow fights at range instead of melee; there's no separate "archer" type, ranged is simply a consequence of the weapon drawn. The same soldier who closed to melee last night might hang back with a bow the next.      Every upgrade is a real risk!      Gear doesn't just get better with gold — it gets  rarer . Pushing a weapon or piece of armor toward its cap means gambling gol

about: Your desktop is the aquarium   fih is a desktop companion game where fish grow beside you while you work. They swim on a transparent window over your whole screen, but every click that does not land on a fish, a pellet, a shark or the UI passes straight through to the window behind. It never gets in your way.   Your typing is the food  Every keypress and click counts as one input. Every 30 inputs, a pellet drops with a little pop. Hungry fish swim over, eat, gain weight, and grow from egg to baby, child, teen and adult. Grown fish earn gold every ten seconds — five minutes of a fish's passive income adds up to its own sell price, so the tank keeps working while you are away. No fish ever starves to death.   Roll, collect, raise  Three kinds of eggs hatch 29 species: 10 ornamental fish, 10 mid-size edible fish, 5 legendary rarities such as the coelacanth, and 4 unique memes (CatFih, ShoesFih, Dih, SelFih). On top of the species roll, every individual rolls its own rarity. The base art is a black crayon sketch on white paper, and rarer individuals get colored over it — pale blue for rare, gold for legendary, a shifting rainbow for unique. Hatch a species once and it unlocks in the collection.   Draw your own fish  An in-game paint panel lets you draw a fish's look yourself. Keep several looks per species in its gallery, and newly hatched fish will wear one of them at random.   Sharks show up  Every 8 to 15 minutes a warning blinks at the edge of the screen and a police siren wails. Your adults swim in to fight; click the shark to add damage. Kill it for a growing reward, or lose fish if you are slow. This is the only place in the game where you can lose anything.   Eight upgrades  Passive income, sell income, feeding rate, food value, auto-clicks per second, rare chance, tank capacity, and combat power.   Pick your monitors  Choose which displays the fish may roam, and they will swim from one monitor to the next. Korean and English are supported, and the aquarium hides itself when a fullscreen app takes over.   Privacy  The global input hook counts events and nothing else. Which keys you pressed is never stored, logged, or sent anywhere.

A herd on the side of your screen          Ledge Goats lives in a tall, narrow strip on the left or right edge of your desktop. It stays on top, and clicks on the empty sky pass through to whatever is underneath. The goats hop from ledge to ledge by themselves. Look over whenever you like. There is always a goat doing something.  Look over, pick an upgrade, get back to work          Every metre a goat climbs is yours to spend. Every so often, spend it on one of six upgrades: more goats, faster climbing, steadier feet on rough rock, warm coats for wind and snow, calls that keep the herd moving in fog, or better grazing. It takes a click or two, and then you can look away again.  Camps, summits and the next mountain          Every peak has four camps on the way to the top. The first one, Kosciuszko, takes about a workday. The peaks get taller as you go, up to Everest, which takes about a working week. At each summit the herd settles on that mountain and you earn a permanent bonus. Then you start the next peak with a small new herd. The Outfit System:  Save your edits and instantly swap between customized looks on the fly.     Mesh & Material Editing:  Toggle specific clothing meshes on or off and swap materials using built-in preset shaders. short: A small illustrated writer sits in the corner of your screen and works on a book of their own, but only while you type. Their published books pay out ink you can spend on new writers. Writelings counts your keystrokes and never records which keys.
about: A writer on your desktop  Writelings is a desktop companion for Windows. A small illustrated writer sits at a desk in a corner of your screen, on top of whatever you're writing in: Word, Google Docs, an email, code, anything.  They're working on a book of their own, and they only write while you type. Stop, and they look up and think for a while before they doze off. Start typing again and so do they. They can't write their masterpiece without you.  Books and ink  Books come in sizes, from a 500-word short story to tomes that run into the millions of words. When your writer finishes one, it goes on their shelf and pays royalties in ink. The whole backlist keeps paying, including for several hours after you close the app.  Writers  You start with the Night Owl, who writes at a lamp-lit desk under the stars. Ink buys new writers, and the cast keeps growing. Each one comes with a whole lit scene of their own:    A frog wizard on a lily pad under a paper lantern    A raftsman on the Mississippi before dawn    A Victorian postmaster mouse working by a thimble of candlelight    A tortoise writing in a glasshouse in flat daylight    A small cloud in a beret, writing the weather into an almanac    A pink slime in a dungeon, writing up the adventurers he ate. He's lit from the inside by the wizard's crystal he swallowed. His desk is a shield on a sword and his pen is an arrow.    Some of them quote their favorite authors while they work. Two stay locked until you've written 80,000 words of your own.  Staying out of the way  Clicks pass through the writer to whatever is underneath. Drag them anywhere and resize them. The panel above them holds their current book, your stats, the shelf, and the shop. It comes in different interface skins, dark and light, so you can pick whichever works best on your screen. Hide it and it's just the writer at their desk.  How it knows you're typing  Windows tells Writelings each time a key goes down, and Writelings adds one to a count. That count is the only input.    It never records which key was pressed, so your words are never read or stored.    It doesn't look at which program or window you're in, or what your documents are called.    Nothing about your typing leaves your computer. There are no analytics and no telemetry.    There are no accounts and no launcher, and nothing runs online. Your progress is one save file on your own computer. Writelings is built with Electron, so its code ships readable in the install folder if you want to check.

short: Tend a living beehive right on your desk. Harvest honey through the seasons, expand your apiary, build a processing line, and automate the work while you're away. A cozy idle beekeeping sim that runs beside you.
about: Desk Hive is a gentle idle beekeeping sim that lives on your desktop while you do other things. You start with one hive, a smoker, and some bees. Over time you grow more colonies, upgrade your equipment, and slowly automate the whole operation. The bees keep working when you close the game.  Gameplay  Each hive runs in real time. Workers forage, honey fills up the supers, and new bees hatch from brood frames. Every colony has a queen with her own traits that affect how fast the hive grows and how much honey it makes. You can upgrade brood boxes to raise worker capacity, install more frames to improve efficiency, and keep sugar feed stocked so the bees don't starve when winter arrives.  Seasons change every six hours whether you're playing or not. Spring is good for building up your workforce. Summer brings the strongest nectar flow. Autumn slows everything down and it's your last chance to stock supplies. Winter is harsh: nectar drops to nearly nothing, brood production grinds to a halt, and every hive burns through sugar feed just to stay alive. A full year cycles in 24 real hours.          The production chain  When a honey super is full, you use the smoker to calm the hive, harvest the frames, and queue extractor jobs to spin raw honey into bulk product. Better extractors process bigger batches and run more jobs at once. Once you own two hives, you unlock jarring stations that package bulk honey into jars worth a lot more money. Sell the jars, sell the wax, reinvest in your apiary.  Upgrades come in three tiers: brood boxes for colony size, extractors for processing speed, and jarring stations for packaging throughput. You can also add more honey supers per hive and install extra brood frames to squeeze out more efficiency.          Automation  Seven automation upgrades let you step back from the busywork as your apiary grows. Auto smoke keeps harvest ready hives calm. Extractor loader harvests and queues extraction jobs on its own. Collector tray grabs finished extractor output. Sales contract sells off excess honey when storage gets full. Supply clerk restocks jars and sugar feed at thresholds you set. Jar line assistant keeps packaging batches running. Apiary supervisor extends everything across hives you're not currently watching.  Offline progress  Close the game and everything keeps running. The simulation covers up to 36 real hours while you're gone, the first 12 at full speed and then gradually slower. When you come back you get a summary of what your bees made: honey produced, jars filled, wax collected, money earned, jobs finished.  No pressure  There's no fail state. If you forget to stock sugar feed before winter, your colonies just slow way down. They don't die. Check in when you feel like it, queue up some jobs, tweak your automation, and let the bees do the rest.

short: A tiny party lives on your desktop in this idle RPG. Your heroes fight monsters and find treasure while you work or browse. Choose their gear and watch them grow into new forms. Take a break to pet them or play with toys. Sometimes it rains frogs.
about: Your party travels through forests, ruins and snowy paths along the edge of your screen. They fight the monsters they meet and collect treasure as they go. You choose who joins the party and how they are equipped.  A life between battles                  After a few battles, your heroes set up camp. They share food, sort their treasure and act out stories for each other. When they are ready, they pack up and carry on.  Watch them grow          As your heroes learn their professions, they earn new forms and tools. You choose which looks each hero wears, and earlier forms stay available. After completing a world, you can take the party into a new one, keeping your heroes, gear and collection. Completed worlds also earn trophies to display beside the party.  Build your party          Discover eight professions and choose a role for each hero. Some attack while others guard or heal. Their spells and equipment change how they fight, so you can try new combinations as your collection grows. The battles play themselves.  Pick them up and play          Pet a hero, give them a toss or throw a paper glider for them to chase. Toys bounce and spin around the party. Frogs and treasure chests can fall from above, landing among your heroes as they react.          Make room on your desktop  Put the party along the bottom or side of your screen and change its size to suit your desktop. Click through empty space to use the programs behind it. A hotkey switches on gaming mode so the whole game ignores the mouse.  Your day can help them grow  Optional activity sensing lets your daily computer use help matching heroes grow. Coding helps the Rune Coder, writing helps the Quill Knight, and typing can speed up battles. All sensing stays on your PC. The game never records what you type. You can switch sensing off and unlock every profession through adventure.  Come back when you like  Chests open themselves and gear is sorted for you. If the party loses a battle, they recover on safer ground and keep going. They can earn progress while the game is closed, with a summary waiting when you return. A weekly pixel card records their adventures for you to save and share.

short: Nothing beats a company-paid holiday! Perfect attendance earned you an unlimited vacation—100% savings on hotels and restaurants, because there are none. Give up and crawl back to work, or survive the wild. A cozy desktop idle survival game. Endure your way to the top.
about: [MEMO: TO ALL VACATIONING EMPLOYEES]     Congratulations on your Perfect Attendance Award. Please read the following notice carefully.     1. Please Enjoy Your Vacation at Your Desk     Chief Endurance Officer is a semi-automatic wilderness survival game that lives quietly in the corner of your work screen. Eight hours at the office equals five full days in the wild. You only need to make a few key decisions during work breaks: Where to explore today? Reinforce the camp? What tools to craft?—The rest of the time, your character will do the hard work for you.     2. Pins Are Distributed According to Labor—Eat More, Earn More     Pins are your action points in the wilderness. Each morning, use pins to plan your day: up to three, one each for morning, midday, and afternoon. Where do pins come from? From last night's dinner—want to get more done tomorrow? Eat more tonight.     3. A Destination You Can Trust     First stop: the mountains of Guangzhou, China. You will be staying in a panoramic eco-suite, with all ingredients freshly caught and gathered, unlimited servings—every plant and animal is drawn from reality, researched and verified one by one.    The more you know about real-world materials and bushcraft, the better tools you'll craft and the more "surprise events" you'll survive. And if you know absolutely nothing about the outdoors? No worries—a few missed meals and you'll figure it out.     4. Diversified Performance Reviews     The longer you endure, the closer you get to the legendary title of Chief Endurance Officer. Of course, endurance isn't everything. The company encourages well-rounded development: Chief Casualty Officer, Chief Starvation Officer, Chief Toxicology Officer, Chief Electrocution Officer—welcome to the C-suite.     5. Team Building Is Permitted     You may invite up to four friends to "vacation" together. Most days, you'll each be enduring on your own; when your paths cross, take a photo, trade journals. And in a true emergency, you may send out a distress call—after all, hard times reveal true friends.    The company reserves the right of final interpretation of this notice. Enjoy your vacation.

name: Game in Picture
lang: English
short: Game in Picture (GiP) is a desktop companion app that keeps your game visible in a picture-in-picture overlay when you Alt+Tab, with manual source controls, audio management, process freezing for single-player games, and customizable themes.
about: Game in Picture (GiP) is a picture-in-picture desktop companion app built for players who frequently switch contexts. Instead of losing awareness when you Alt+Tab, GiP keeps a live view of your game visible in a compact overlay so you never miss the action. With manual source controls, audio management, process freezing for single-player games, and customizable themes, GiP makes interruptions less punishing and helps you return to the action faster with fewer missed moments.   Your game, your rules!         GiP is designed for games running in Borderless Fullscreen (also known as Windowed Fullscreen).   Four ways GiP can help  GiP keeps your game within reach when you step away from full-screen play.            Pause When You Need To   Pause and resume supported single-player or offline games directly from GiP when you need to step away. Auto-pause can be enabled separately for each game, allowing GiP to pause it when you leave fullscreen and resume it when you return. Before pausing software with online capabilities or active network traffic, GiP displays a warning so you can decide whether it is safe to continue.  GiP does not modify memory or touch save data. It does not rely on the game’s built-in pause system. Instead, it temporarily suspends the game process, freezing the game exactly where it is, even if the game has no pause function of its own.        Media and Audio Controls in One Place   Control the tracked application’s sound without opening the Windows volume mixer. Click the audio control to mute or unmute, then drag around it to adjust volume. Auto-mute can silence the tracked window whenever you switch away and restore its sound when you return. For recognized browsers and media players, GiP also provides play/pause and previous/next commands when the application supports them.         Manual Source Control   By default, GiP automatically follows the fullscreen window you Alt+Tab away from. When you want tighter control, Explicit Tracking only changes the source when you hold the backtick key while Alt+Tabbing, while Manual Selection lets you choose a specific eligible window from the source list.   Manual Mode   Choose exactly which window GiP follows whenever you want direct control. Switch between your game, a browser, a guide, a video, or another app without rebuilding your overlay, then keep the selected source visible over the fullscreen application you are using.   Pin Mode   Keep GiP visible over fullscreen windows. Move between fullscreen apps while GiP shows the window you switched away from; when using Manual Source Control, your selected source remains fixed.         Themes and Visual Style   Match GiP to the rest of your setup with a selection of visual themes. Each theme updates the interface consistently while preserving clear controls and readable information across different games and desktop environments.         Flexible Overlay Placement   Resize and position GiP to suit your screen, game, and workspace. Keep the overlay locked in a corner, move it wherever it avoids important on-screen information, or use a compact floating layout that stays useful without taking over your display.         Expanded View Mode   Double-click GiP to switch between Normal View and Expanded View. Expanded View gives more of the window to the captured image and keeps surrounding interface elements out of the way. Move the pointer over GiP whenever you need its title bar or controls again. A separate Fullscreen option from the context menu can expand GiP across the entire display.         Tray Integration and Quick Access   Keep GiP available for long sessions without adding unnecessary desktop clutter. Send it to the system tray when it is not needed, restore it quickly, and use convenient tray actions to reach common controls and capture options.
